note.explanation: Power tells us how quickly work is done or energy is transferred. To find power, divide the work done by the time taken.
examples: If 100 J of work is done in 5 s, the power is 100/5 = 20 W.
A machine that transfers 600 J of energy in 3 s has power 600/3 = 200 W.
note.checkAnswer: Power = work done ÷ time taken; P = W/t.
note.simple: Power is how fast work is done.
note.checkQuestion: A machine does 120 J of work in 6 s. What is its power?
note.title: Finding power
steps: Put the work done, W, and time taken, t, into the formula.
Write the answer in watts (W), unless another unit is requested.

mcqs.stem: A machine does 300 J of work in 5 s. Its power is:
rationales: 12 W is incorrect because it does not equal 300 J divided by 5 s.
60 W is correct because P = W/t = 300/5 = 60 W.
120 W is incorrect because it would result from dividing 300 J by 2.5 s.
720 W is incorrect because it is not the work divided by the given time.

mcqs.stem: What is the SI unit of power?
rationales: A joule is the SI unit of work and energy, not power.
A newton is the SI unit of force, not power.
A watt is the SI unit of power.
A metre is the SI unit of length, not power.
1 J s⁻¹ is correct because one watt is one joule of work done per second.
1 J s is incorrect because it multiplies joules by seconds rather than dividing by time.
1 N s⁻¹ is incorrect because it is not the definition of a watt.
1 kg m s⁻¹ is incorrect because these units do not represent power.
10² W is 100 W, not one kilowatt.
10³ W is correct because 1 kW = 1000 W.
10⁴ W is 10,000 W, which is more than one kilowatt.
10⁶ W is one megawatt, not one kilowatt.

mcqs.stem: According to the section, one horse-power is equal to:
rationales: 746 W is correct because 1 hp = 746 W.
1000 W is one kilowatt, not one horse-power.
1200 W is not the stated conversion for one horse-power.
2500 W is not the stated conversion for one horse-power.

mcqs.stem: Power is a scalar quantity because:
rationales: Scalar is correct because work and time are scalar quantities, and power is their ratio.
Vector is incorrect because power has no direction.
Neither scalar nor vector is incorrect because power is a scalar quantity.
Always negative is incorrect because power is not defined as a quantity that must be negative.

written.text: Q5.3. A force F₁ does 5 J of work in 10 s. Another force F₂ does 3 J of work in 5 s. Which force delivers greater power?
written.finalAnswer: F₂ delivers greater power: 0.6 W compared with 0.5 W for F₁.

rubric.why: The power of the first force must be calculated for comparison.
rubric.description: Find the power delivered by F₁.
rubric.how: Use P = W/t to get P₁ = 0.5 W.

rubric.why: The second force delivers greater power only if its calculated rate is larger.
rubric.description: Find the power delivered by F₂ and compare.
rubric.how: Use P = W/t to get P₂ = 0.6 W, so F₂ delivers greater power.

modelAnswer: From P = W/t, power delivered by F₁ = 5 J/10 s = 0.5 W
Power delivered by F₂ = 3 J/5 s = 0.6 W

written.text: Q5.9. What is power? Define the unit used for it.
written.finalAnswer: Power is the time rate of doing work. Its SI unit is the watt (W); one watt is the work done at the rate of one joule per second.

written.text: Q5.11. A force of 600 N acts on a box to push it 5 m in 15 s. Calculate the power.

rubric.why: Work done is needed before power can be found.
rubric.description: Calculate the work done on the box.
rubric.how: Use W = FS to find 3000 J.

rubric.why: Power is determined from work and time.
rubric.how: Use P = W/t with W = 3000 J and t = 15 s.

rubric.why: The answer must state the calculated power with its unit.

modelAnswer: Work done, W = FS = 600 N × 5 m = 3000 J
From P = W/t, P = 3000 J/15 s = 200 W

written.text: Q5.12. A 40 kg boy runs up-stair 10 m high in 8 s. What power he developed.

rubric.why: The boy does work by gaining gravitational potential energy.
rubric.description: Calculate the work done in climbing the stairs.
rubric.how: Use W = mgh with g = 10 m s⁻² to find 4000 J.

rubric.why: The work must be related to the time taken.
rubric.how: Use P = W/t and substitute 4000 J and 8 s.

rubric.why: The final power must be calculated and given with its unit.

modelAnswer: Taking g = 10 m s⁻², work done, W = mgh
From P = W/t, P = 4000 J/8 s = 500 W

explain.title: What power means
explain.body: Power is defined as the time rate of doing work. It tells us how quickly work is done. Doing the same work in less time means greater power.

explain.title: The formula for power
explain.body: If W is the work done in time t, then P = W/t. Power of any agency can also be defined as energy transferred per unit time.

explain.title: The watt
explain.body: One watt is the work done at the rate of one joule per second. So, 1 W = 1 J/1 s or 1 J s⁻¹. Power is a scalar quantity.

explain.title: Larger units
explain.body: The larger units are 1 kW = 10³ W and 1 MW = 10⁶ W. The horse-power conversion given in your textbook is 1 hp = 746 W.

explain.title: Finding power in a numerical
explain.body: First find the work if it is not given. For a constant force along the displacement, use W = FS. Then divide the work by the time: P = W/t.

mistakes: Using P = t/W instead of P = W/t.
Forgetting to calculate the work first when the question gives force and distance.
Writing the answer without a power unit such as W or kW.
Mixing up joules, which measure work or energy, with watts, which measure power.
Converting kilowatts incorrectly; 1 kW = 1000 W, not 100 W.
Using the wrong time unit or forgetting to divide by the time taken.
